_meta.purpose: The teacher's facilitation guide: a 45 minute lesson in six blocks, each with what students do, what to say and what to watch for. Written for a form teacher or an ECG lesson with a class that holds G1, G2 and G3 in the same room.
_meta.source: Authored for this app. The order follows the three questions of MOE's Education and Career Guidance: Who am I? Where do I want to go? How do I get there?
_meta.notes: The guide never asks a teacher to compare students. The app shows no count of places, and the guide asks teachers to keep it that way in the room.

before: Open Paths once on each device while on school wifi. After that it works with no signal.
Make a class play code on this page and write it on the board.
Open the projector view on the classroom screen.
Nothing is collected. Each plan stays on that student's device.

frame.head: One class, every level
lines: Your class holds G1, G2 and G3 in the same subject. Each of the 8 places is a path in its own right.
Start from each student's goal. Do not ask who has more places on track.
A move up is an option. For a student whose levels fit their goal, the work is doing well where they are.

blocks.do: Two taps on what they enjoy. One strength, with one line of what shows it.
blocks.say: There are no right answers here. Nobody sees this unless you share it.
blocks.watch: Students copying a neighbour. Ask each one what shows their strength.

blocks.do: They set their real levels for this year.
blocks.say: A level describes a subject this year. It does not describe you.
blocks.watch: Levels entered as wishes. Both are fine. Ask which it is.

blocks.do: One goal, and one line of why.
blocks.say: Pick the place that fits what you wrote on Me. You can change it next week.
blocks.watch: Goals chosen for status. Ask about the work, then the place.

blocks.do: The short story, once through, with the class code.
blocks.say: Everyone meets the same chances. Your choices are what differ.
blocks.watch: Racing to the end. Slow the room down at results day.

blocks.do: In pairs, then the room. Use the debrief questions below.
blocks.say: Tell your partner one thing your story showed you about yourself.
blocks.watch: Comparing routes as better or worse. Bring it back to fit.

blocks.do: One step, one date, one adult to tell.
blocks.say: Choose one step you will do this term.
blocks.watch: Lists of five steps. One done is worth more.

debrief.q: What did you assume was closed to you that turned out to have a route in?
debrief.why: Surfaces beliefs picked up from siblings and from adults schooled under streams.

debrief.q: What did your starting levels decide, and what did they leave open?
debrief.why: The question the lesson turns on. Give it ten minutes.

debrief.q: Whose goal looks nothing like yours, and what does it ask of them?
debrief.why: Each path asks for something. None is the easy one.

debrief.q: What went wrong in your story, and what happened after it?
debrief.why: Treats a setback as an event with a next step.

after: Next week, ask each student about their one step.
For a student who wants more time, the 15 minute session below takes the same order.
A parent can open a card the student shares. It carries only what the student chose.
